name: Engineering Physics Lab
objectives: To introduce the hands-on descriptions of various physical concepts of optics, mechanics, thermal physics etc. with the help of related instruments and devices.
outcomes: To formulate, analyze and solve multilevel laboratory problems in electromagnetism.
To demonstrate experimental comprehension of electric and magnetic field based systems.
To analyze the physical principle involved in various instruments.
To handle various experiments in the area of optics, mechanics and thermal physics.
To think innovatively and improve the creative skills that are essential for engineers.
note:
Record format: aim, apparatus, circuit or ray diagram, formula with unit of every symbol, observation table with least count, calculation of one full reading, result with percentage error, precautions.
Draw graphs on graph paper with labelled axes, units and scale, and read the slope from a large triangle, not from two data points.
Before each viva, memorise the formula, the meaning of every symbol, the SI unit of the answer and the two main sources of error.

exps.title: To determine the wavelength and fringe widths of sodium light by Young's double slit experiment
exps.aim: Find the fringe width and the wavelength of sodium light from the interference pattern of two coherent slits.
exps.apparatus: Sodium lamp, double slit, convex lens, micrometer eyepiece, optical bench
exps.formula: β = λD/d, so λ = βd/D (D = slit to screen distance, d = slit separation). Sodium D-line about 589.3 nm.
viva: Why are two separate lamps not used as the two sources?
Independent sources are not coherent; phase difference changes randomly, so no stable fringes form.
What is the condition for a bright fringe?
Path difference equals nλ, where n is an integer (0, 1, 2 ...).
What happens to fringe width if the whole set-up is placed in water?
Wavelength reduces to λ/μ, so the fringe width decreases by the factor μ.

exps.title: To determine the wavelength of sodium light by Newton's rings
exps.aim: Find λ from the diameters of dark rings formed between a plano-convex lens and a glass plate.
exps.apparatus: Sodium lamp, plano-convex lens, optical flat, travelling microscope, glass plate at 45°
exps.formula: λ = (D²ₙ₊ₚ − D²ₙ)/(4pR), D = ring diameter, R = radius of curvature of the lens.
viva: Why is the centre of the ring system dark in reflected light?
A phase change of π occurs on reflection at the glass plate, so the reflected rays cancel at zero air thickness.
Why do rings get closer together outward?
Diameter varies as √n, so the ring spacing shrinks as n increases.
Why is the diameter squared plotted against ring number?
D² = 4nλR, so the plot is a straight line and the slope averages out errors.

exps.title: To determine the wavelength of sodium light (monochromatic source) with the help of Fresnel's biprism
exps.aim: Find λ by measuring fringe width, source-to-screen distance and slit separation of the virtual sources.
exps.apparatus: Fresnel biprism, sodium lamp, adjustable slit, convex lens, optical bench, micrometer eyepiece
exps.formula: λ = βd/D, with d = √(d₁d₂) from the two lens positions giving magnified and diminished images of the slit.
viva: How does a biprism produce coherent sources?
It divides the wavefront of a single slit into two by refraction, giving two virtual coherent images.
Why is the slit kept parallel to the biprism edge?
The two virtual sources must be parallel line sources; otherwise the fringes are blurred or lost.
Why is the biprism angle very small?
The prism has a very obtuse apex angle (about 179°), i.e. base angles of only about 0.5°, so the deviation is small, the virtual sources are close together and the fringes are wide enough to see.

exps.title: To determine the wavelength of He-Ne laser using Michelson-Morley interferometer
exps.aim: Find λ by counting fringes that shift as one mirror of the interferometer is moved a known distance.
exps.apparatus: He-Ne laser, Michelson interferometer, beam splitter, compensating plate, micrometer screw, screen
exps.formula: λ = 2d/N, d = mirror displacement, N = number of fringes crossing the reference point. He-Ne is 632.8 nm.
viva: Why is the mirror displacement d related to 2d/λ fringes?
The beam travels the extra path twice, so path change is 2d; each λ of path change shifts one fringe.
What is the purpose of the compensating plate?
It makes the glass path equal in both arms, which is needed for white-light fringes and keeps the path difference the same for all wavelengths.
What kind of fringes appear with a laser and parallel mirrors?
Circular fringes of equal inclination are seen when the mirrors are nearly perpendicular.

exps.title: To determine the separation between the plates of a Fabry-Perot etalon and the order of interference at the centre of Fabry-Perot fringes
exps.aim: Find the etalon spacing d and central-fringe order from the measured ring diameters.
exps.apparatus: Fabry-Perot etalon, sodium or mercury source, convex lens, telescope or travelling microscope, screen
exps.formula: 2d cosθ = nλ; central order n = 2d/λ. For a close doublet, d = λ₁λ₂/[2(λ₁ − λ₂)].
viva: How does a Fabry-Perot etalon differ from a Michelson interferometer?
It uses multiple-beam interference, giving much sharper fringes than the two-beam Michelson.
What is the free spectral range?
Δλ = λ²/2d, the largest wavelength range without order overlap.
Why are the rings sharp and narrow?
Many partially reflected beams add up; only near-exact phase matching gives a bright maximum.

exps.title: To determine the specific rotation of cane sugar solution with the help of polarimeter
exps.aim: Measure the optical rotation of sugar solutions of known concentration and find the specific rotation.
exps.apparatus: Laurent half-shade polarimeter, sodium lamp, polarimeter tube, cane sugar solutions, balance
exps.formula: [α] = θ/(l·c), θ = rotation (degrees), l = tube length (dm), c = concentration (g/cm³).
viva: What is specific rotation?
Rotation produced by a 1 dm tube containing 1 g/cm³ of the optically active solution at a given wavelength and temperature.
Why is a half-shade device used?
Matching two half-fields to equal brightness is far more sensitive than judging the darkest position.
Is cane sugar dextro- or laevorotatory?
Dextrorotatory; it rotates the plane of polarisation clockwise.

exps.title: To determine the wavelength of prominent spectral lines of mercury light by plane diffraction grating
exps.aim: Find λ of the violet, green and yellow mercury lines using a spectrometer and a grating.
exps.apparatus: Spectrometer, plane diffraction grating, mercury vapour lamp, spirit level, reading lens
exps.formula: nλ = (a + b) sinθ, and (a + b) = 1/N (grating element = 1/lines per unit length).
viva: What is the grating element?
The distance (a + b) between the centres of two adjacent slits, equal to 1/N.
Why is normal incidence adjusted before measurement?
The formula nλ = (a + b) sinθ holds only when light falls normal to the grating.
What limits the maximum order observable?
sinθ cannot exceed 1, so n ≤ (a + b)/λ.

exps.title: To determine the numerical aperture of an optical fiber
exps.aim: Measure the acceptance cone of a fibre and calculate its numerical aperture.
exps.apparatus: Optical fibre with light source, NA measurement jig with screen, metre scale, power supply
exps.formula: NA = sinθ₀ = r/√(r² + L²) = √(n₁² − n₂²), r = spot radius, L = fibre-screen distance.
viva: What is the numerical aperture?
The sine of the maximum acceptance angle; it measures the light-gathering ability of the fibre.
Why must the core index exceed the cladding index?
Total internal reflection at the core-cladding boundary needs light moving from denser to rarer medium.
What is the acceptance angle?
The maximum angle to the axis at which incident light is still guided by total internal reflection.

exps.title: To determine the wavelength of given laser by plane diffraction grating
exps.aim: Find the laser wavelength from the diffraction orders on a screen.
exps.apparatus: Laser source, plane diffraction grating, screen, metre scale, stand
exps.formula: nλ = d sinθ, sinθ = x/√(x² + L²), d = 1/N (x = order position, L = grating-screen distance).
viva: Why are laser spots sharp and well separated?
The laser is highly monochromatic and collimated, so each order forms a narrow spot at a fixed angle.
How would you get more orders on the screen?
Use a grating with a larger line spacing (fewer lines per mm), or a shorter laser wavelength.
What safety precaution is essential?
Never look into the beam or its reflection; avoid mirror-like objects in its path.

exps.title: To determine the resolving power of a telescope
exps.aim: Find the resolving power of a telescope for different aperture widths using a distant pair of objects.
exps.apparatus: Telescope with adjustable slit, two distant thin vertical lines, metre scale, travelling microscope
exps.formula: Minimum resolvable angle dθ = 1.22λ/a for a circular aperture and dθ = λ/a for the rectangular slit used in this experiment; R.P. = 1/dθ (a = aperture width). Experimentally dθ = s/L.
viva: State the Rayleigh criterion.
Two point sources are just resolved when the central maximum of one falls on the first minimum of the other.
How can the resolving power be increased?
Increase the objective aperture or use a shorter wavelength.
Why do astronomers build large-diameter telescopes?
Both light gathering and resolving power increase with the aperture.

exps.title: To determine the resistance per unit length of Carey Foster's bridge wire and to determine the specific resistance of a given wire
exps.aim: Find the resistance per unit length of the bridge wire, then use it to find an unknown resistance and the specific resistance of a wire.
exps.apparatus: Carey Foster bridge, standard resistances, resistance box, galvanometer, battery, jockey, unknown wire, screw gauge
exps.formula: X − Y = ρ(l₂ − l₁) (ρ = resistance per unit length, l₁, l₂ = balance lengths before and after interchange); specific resistance = Xπr²/L.
viva: Why are the end resistances not needed?
Interchanging the resistances cancels the unknown end resistances, which is the key property of the Carey Foster method.
Why should the ratio arms P and Q be nearly equal?
Balance then falls near the middle of the wire, where sensitivity and uniformity are best.
Why is the jockey not slid along the wire?
Sliding damages the wire and changes its uniform cross-section.

exps.title: To determine the variation of magnetic field along the axis of a current carrying coil and then to estimate the radius of the coil
exps.aim: Plot the axial field of a circular coil against distance and use the points of inflexion to estimate the coil radius.
exps.apparatus: Stewart and Gee apparatus (tangent galvanometer type), rheostat, ammeter, battery, commutator, compass needle
exps.formula: B = μ₀nIa²/[2(a² + x²)^{3/2}]. The graph has inflexion points at x = ±a/2, separated by a.
viva: State the Biot-Savart law.
dB = (μ₀/4π) I dl sinθ / r²; field due to a current element varies inversely as the square of distance.
What is the field at the centre of a circular coil?
B = μ₀nI/2a, where n is the number of turns and a is the radius.
Why is the reading reversed by the commutator?
Reversing the current and averaging the readings removes errors from imperfect alignment of the coil and needle, zero error and pivot friction.

exps.title: To draw the hysteresis curve and hysteresis loss of a given ferromagnetic sample and from this to determine magnetic susceptibility and permeability: (i) obtain the B-H curve on a C.R.O. using a solenoid and determine the related magnetic constants; (ii) determine hysteresis loss using C.R.O.
exps.aim: Display the B-H loop on a CRO, find retentivity, coercivity, permeability, susceptibility and the loss per cycle.
exps.apparatus: CRO, solenoid with specimen, integrating circuit (R, C), resistances, AC supply, transformer
exps.formula: Energy loss per unit volume per cycle = area of the B-H loop; μ = B/H and χ = μ/μ₀ − 1 = μᵣ − 1.
viva: Why does the area of the loop represent energy loss?
Work done per unit volume per cycle is the integral of H dB, which equals the enclosed loop area.
Which loop suits a transformer core, and why?
A narrow loop of soft iron, since it has low coercivity and low hysteresis loss.
Define retentivity and coercivity.
Retentivity is the flux density left when H = 0; coercivity is the reverse field needed to bring B to zero.

exps.title: To calibrate a given voltmeter and ammeter by means of a potentiometer
exps.aim: Check the readings of a voltmeter and ammeter against the potentiometer and draw calibration curves.
exps.apparatus: Potentiometer, accumulator, standard cell, voltmeter, ammeter, rheostat, standard resistance, galvanometer, key
exps.formula: E₁/E₂ = l₁/l₂; potential gradient k = V/L; true p.d. = k·l; true current I = V/R across a standard resistor.
viva: Why is a potentiometer preferred to a voltmeter for measuring e.m.f.?
At balance it draws no current from the cell, so it measures the true e.m.f., not the terminal voltage.
What is the potential gradient?
The fall in potential per unit length of the potentiometer wire.
What does a calibration curve show?
The error (true − observed) against the reading, used to correct the instrument.

exps.title: To study the Hall effect and determine Hall coefficient, carrier density and mobility of a given semiconductor material using Hall effect set up
exps.aim: Measure the Hall voltage, find the Hall coefficient, sign and density of charge carriers and the mobility.
exps.apparatus: Hall effect apparatus, semiconductor Hall probe, electromagnet with power supply, gaussmeter, constant-current source, digital millivoltmeter
exps.formula: R_H = V_H t/(I B) = 1/(ne); n = 1/(e R_H); mobility μ = |R_H|σ.
viva: What is the Hall effect?
A transverse voltage appears across a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field perpendicular to the current.
What can be found from the sign of the Hall voltage?
The type of majority carriers: negative R_H for electrons (n-type), positive for holes (p-type).
Why is the Hall voltage larger in semiconductors than in metals?
V_H is proportional to 1/n, and carrier density in semiconductors is much smaller.

exps.title: To determine the resistivity and energy band gap of a semiconductor (germanium) using the four probe method; (ii) to determine the band gap in a semiconductor using a PN junction diode
exps.aim: Find resistivity and band gap from the temperature dependence of resistance of a Ge crystal, and cross-check with a PN diode.
exps.apparatus: Four probe apparatus, Ge crystal, oven with thermometer, constant-current source, millivoltmeter, PN junction diode
exps.formula: ρ = ρ₀/G(w/s), ρ₀ = (V/I)·2πs; Eg = 2k × slope of ln ρ against 1/T. For the diode, the slope of ln I₀ against 1/T gives Eg = k × slope.
viva: Why are four probes used instead of two?
The current probes carry the current while the voltage probes draw none, so contact resistance is removed.
What is the band gap of Ge?
About 0.67 eV at room temperature.
How does the resistance of an intrinsic semiconductor change with temperature?
It falls exponentially because more carriers are excited across the band gap.

exps.title: To determine the V-I characteristics of a diode and determine the energy gap of the semiconductor
exps.aim: Plot forward and reverse V-I curves, find the knee voltage and dynamic resistance, and deduce the band gap.
exps.apparatus: PN junction diode, DC supply, rheostat, voltmeter, milliammeter, microammeter, heating arrangement, thermometer
exps.formula: I = I₀[exp(eV/ηkT) − 1]; dynamic resistance r = ΔV/ΔI; band gap from the temperature variation of reverse saturation current I₀ ∝ exp(−Eg/kT).
viva: What are the knee voltages of Ge and Si diodes?
About 0.3 V for germanium and 0.7 V for silicon.
How does temperature affect the reverse saturation current?
It roughly doubles for every 10 °C rise because minority carriers increase.
Why is a series resistance used in forward bias?
To limit the current below the rated value and avoid burning the diode.

exps.title: To study V-I characteristics of LED and laser sources and hence to determine the responsivity of a photo receiver
exps.aim: Plot V-I curves of an LED and a laser diode, and find the receiver's response to optical power.
exps.apparatus: LED, laser diode, photodiode or photo receiver, DC supply, voltmeter, microammeter, optical power meter
exps.formula: Responsivity R = I_ph/P (A/W); threshold voltage found from the forward-characteristic knee.
viva: How does an LED emit light?
Electrons recombine with holes in the forward-biased junction and release photons (spontaneous emission).
What is responsivity of a photodetector?
The photocurrent produced per unit incident optical power, in A/W.
How does laser emission differ from LED emission?
A laser uses stimulated emission and gives coherent, narrow, directional light.

exps.title: To measure the optical loss, fibre length and hence determine the attenuation coefficient of an optical fibre at different wavelengths and to find the radius of curvature of the optical fibre
exps.aim: Measure power loss over fibre length to find the attenuation coefficient, and examine loss due to bending.
exps.apparatus: Optical fibre spools of known length, LED sources of different wavelengths, optical power meter, mandrels of known radius
exps.formula: α (dB/km) = (10/L) log₁₀(P_in/P_out); bending increases the loss as the radius of curvature falls.
viva: What is attenuation in a fibre?
Loss of optical power with distance, measured in dB/km.
Name two causes of fibre loss.
Absorption and Rayleigh scattering (also bending and connector losses).
Which wavelengths are used in fibre communication?
The low-loss windows near 850 nm, 1310 nm and 1550 nm.

exps.title: Comparison of P-I characteristics of LED and ILD and hence determine the region of operations and laser threshold current
exps.aim: Plot optical power against drive current for an LED and an injection laser diode, and find the threshold current.
exps.apparatus: LED, injection laser diode (ILD), power supply, ammeter, optical power meter, driver circuit
exps.formula: Below threshold the ILD acts like an LED; above the threshold current I_th the output rises steeply. Slope efficiency = ΔP/ΔI.
viva: What is the threshold current of a laser diode?
The current above which stimulated emission dominates and the output rises sharply.
Why is the LED P-I curve nearly linear?
Its output is spontaneous emission, proportional to injected current, with no threshold.
Which source is better for a long-distance fibre link?
ILD, because of its narrow spectrum and high power.

exps.title: To find out the fill factor of a given solar cell
exps.aim: Plot the I-V curve of a solar cell under illumination and find the fill factor and efficiency.
exps.apparatus: Solar cell, light source, rheostat, voltmeter, ammeter, lux meter or intensity meter
exps.formula: FF = (V_m I_m)/(V_oc I_sc); efficiency η = V_m I_m/P_in.
viva: Define fill factor.
Ratio of the maximum power output to the product of open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current.
What is the working principle of a solar cell?
The photovoltaic effect: photons create electron-hole pairs, which the junction field separates.
What is a typical fill factor for silicon cells?
About 0.7 to 0.8.

exps.title: To verify Stefan's law by electrical method
exps.aim: Show that power radiated by a hot filament varies as the fourth power of its absolute temperature.
exps.apparatus: Bulb filament, variable DC supply, voltmeter, ammeter, connecting wires
exps.formula: P = σA(T⁴ − T₀⁴) ∝ T⁴; a log-log plot of P against T has slope 4. T is found from R = R₀[1 + α(T − T₀)].
viva: State Stefan's law.
Energy radiated per unit area per second by a black body is proportional to T⁴.
What is the value of the Stefan-Boltzmann constant?
Why is the filament temperature found from its resistance?
Resistance of a metal varies with temperature in a known way, so R gives T without a pyrometer.

exps.title: To determine the numerical aperture and to evaluate V-number of a given optical fibre
exps.aim: Find the NA of a fibre, then compute the V-number and the number of guided modes.
exps.apparatus: Optical fibre, He-Ne or LED source, NA jig, screen, scale, core radius data
exps.formula: V = (2πa/λ)·NA; single mode if V < 2.405; number of modes ≈ V²/2 for a step-index fibre.
viva: What does the V-number represent?
A normalised frequency that decides how many modes the fibre supports.
What is the condition for single-mode operation?
V must be less than 2.405.
How can a multimode fibre be made single-mode?
Reduce the core radius or the NA, or use a longer wavelength.

exps.title: To determine the susceptibility of paramagnetic solution (Quincke's tube method)
exps.aim: Find the volume susceptibility of a paramagnetic solution from the rise of its column between magnet poles.
exps.apparatus: Quincke's tube, electromagnet, paramagnetic solution (FeCl₃ or MnSO₄), travelling microscope, gaussmeter, power supply
exps.formula: χ = 2ρgh/(μ₀H²) = 2μ₀ρgh/B² (air susceptibility neglected), h = rise of the meniscus.
viva: Why does the liquid level rise in the field?
A paramagnetic liquid is pulled into the region of strong field, so the meniscus rises.
Distinguish diamagnetic and paramagnetic materials.
Diamagnetic materials have small negative χ; paramagnetic materials have small positive χ.
How does paramagnetic susceptibility depend on temperature?
By Curie's law, χ ∝ 1/T.

exps.title: To determine the frequency of A.C. mains with a sonometer using non-magnetic and magnetic wire
exps.aim: Find the mains frequency by adjusting the vibrating length of a wire until it resonates with the AC-driven force (non-magnetic wire carrying the AC in a permanent magnet's field; magnetic wire in the field of an AC electromagnet).
exps.apparatus: Sonometer, non-magnetic wire (brass), magnetic wire (iron or steel), step-down transformer, permanent horseshoe magnet, electromagnet on AC mains, weights, paper rider
exps.formula: Non-magnetic wire (carries the AC through a step-down transformer, placed in a permanent magnet's field): the force reverses every half cycle, so it vibrates at f and f = (1/2l)√(T/m). Magnetic wire (lies in the field of an AC electromagnet): it is attracted in both half cycles, so it vibrates at 2f and f = (1/4l)√(T/m); m = mass per unit length, T = tension.
viva: Why does a magnetic wire vibrate at twice the mains frequency?
The magnet attracts the wire in both half cycles, so the force repeats twice per cycle.
How do you know resonance has been reached?
The paper rider is thrown off or vibrates with maximum amplitude.
What is the mains frequency in India?
50 Hz.

exps.title: To determine the frequency of an electrically maintained tuning fork by Melde's experiment: transverse and longitudinal modes
exps.aim: Find the tuning-fork frequency from the loop length of a vibrating string in both arrangements.
exps.apparatus: Electrically maintained tuning fork, string, pan with weights, pulley, metre scale, balance
exps.formula: Transverse mode (prong vibrates perpendicular to the string): n = (p/2l)√(T/m). Longitudinal mode (prong vibrates along the string): n = (p/l)√(T/m); p = number of loops in length l, T = tension, m = mass per unit length.
viva: Why is the string frequency half the fork frequency in the longitudinal mode?

The prong changes the string tension once per prong vibration, but tension peaks twice per string vibration (at each extreme displacement), so the string makes one vibration for every two of the prong and the fork frequency is twice the string frequency.
How does the loop length depend on tension?
λ ∝ √T, so loops get longer as the tension rises.
Why are stationary waves formed on the string?
The incident and reflected transverse waves superpose to form nodes and antinodes.
